translations.text: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine came upon the land. A man went from Bethlehem in Judah to live in the countryside of Moab, with his wife and his children.

The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the country of Moab and lived there.
Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
They took Moabite wives for themselves. One was named Orpah, and the other was named Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
Both Mahlon and Chilion died, and the woman was left without her husband and her two sons.
She and both her daughters-in-law set out to return from the country of Moab, because she had heard that the Lord had shown mercy to his people by giving them food.
She left the place where they had been living, with both her daughters-in-law accompanying her, and they went along the road toward the land of Judah.
Naomi said to her daughters-in-law, “Go back to your mothers' homes. May the Lord show you his mercy, as you have shown it to those who died and to me.
May the Lord grant that you find rest in the homes of your husbands.” She kissed them, and they cried aloud and wept.
They said to her, “We will return with you to your people.”
Naomi said to them, “Go back, my daughters. Why should you come with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could marry you?
Go back, then, my daughters, for I have grown too old to marry and bear children.

Would you wait for them until they grew up? Would you restrain yourselves and not marry? No, my daughters! My soul has become exceedingly bitter, more so than yours, because the Lord's hand has withdrawn from me.”
They cried aloud again and wept. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.
Naomi said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. You too should return with your sister-in-law.”
Ruth said to her, “Do not urge me to leave you and turn back from following you. Wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you stay, I will stay. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord do this to me, and may this be so: nothing but death will separate me from you.”
When Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her about it.
The two of them went on until they reached Bethlehem. The whole town was stirred because of her, and they said to her, “Are you still alive, Naomi?”
She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for I have become exceedingly bitter.”
“I went away full, but the Lord brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me and caused me such great suffering?”
Naomi returned with Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law. They came from the country of Moab and reached Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
Naomi had a man who was an acquaintance of her husband, a strong and capable man from Elimelech's family. His name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “May I go into the fields and glean grain wherever I find favor?” She said to her, “Go, my daughter.”
She went and gleaned in the fields, following the reapers. She came to a portion of the fields belonging to Boaz, who was a relative of Elimelech.
Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, “The Lord be with you.” They said to him, “May the Lord bless you.”
Boaz said to his young man who was in charge of the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”
The young man who was in charge of the reapers answered, “She is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab.

She said, ‘Let me glean and gather what has fallen from the sheaves behind the reapers.’ She came and remained from morning until evening, and she has not stopped even for a little while in the fields.”
Boaz said to Ruth, “Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave this place. Instead, stay close to my young women.”
Watch the fields where they are reaping, and follow them. Look, I have ordered the young men not to touch you. If you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what the young men have brought.
She fell facedown and bowed to the ground, and said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, take notice of me, for I am a foreigner.”

Boaz answered her, “I have been told everything you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died, and how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth and came to a people you did not know before.”
“May the Lord reward you for what you have done. May you receive your full reward from the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you have come to find refuge under his wings.”
Ruth said to him, “I have found favor in your eyes, for you have made me glad and comforted the heart of your servant. Look, I will be like one of your servant women.”

When it was mealtime, Boaz said to her, “Come here, eat your food, and dip your bread in the vinegar.” Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boaz gathered some ground grain for her. She ate and was satisfied, and had some left over.
She got up to glean, and Boaz instructed his young men, saying, “Let her glean among the sheaves, and do not shame her.”
“Carry some for her from what she has gathered, and leave it for her, so that she may eat and glean it. Do not rebuke her.”
She gleaned in the fields until evening and beat out what she had gathered. The barley amounted to an ephah.
She took it and brought it into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had left over after eating her fill.

Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!” Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had worked, and said to her, “The name of the man with whom I spent the day today is Boaz.”

Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the Lord, for he has not abandoned his kindness toward the living and the dead.” Naomi also said, “The man is our close relative, one of our kinsmen.”
Ruth said to her mother-in-law, “He told me, ‘Stay with my young women until our harvest is finished.’”
Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you stay close to his young women, so that they do not find you in another field.”
Ruth stayed with Boaz’s young women to glean until the barley and wheat harvests were finished, and she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, so that things may go well for you?”
“Now, is not Boaz, whose young women you have been with, our acquaintance? Look, he is working at his threshing floor tonight.”
“Wash yourself, anoint yourself, put on your clothes, and go to his threshing floor. Let no one see you until he has finished eating and drinking.”
“When he lies down, note the place where he sleeps. Then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. He himself will tell you what to do.”
Ruth said to her, “I will do everything you tell me.”
She went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.
Boaz ate, and his heart was cheerful. He went and lay down beside the heap of grain. She came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
At midnight the man woke up, was startled, and found a woman at his feet.
He said to her, “Who are you?” She answered him, “I am Ruth, your servant. Cover me with the edge of your garment, for you are a kinsman.”
Boaz said to her, “May you be blessed by the Lord, my daughter. Your later kindness is greater than your earlier kindness, because you did not go after young men, whether poor or rich.”
“Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you everything you ask. All my people know that you are a woman of worth and that I am a relative with the right to marry you.”
“But there is a relative with the right to marry you who is more closely related than I am.”

“Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he will exercise his right to marry you, good; let him do so. But if he is unwilling to exercise that right, as the Lord lives, I will marry you myself. Stay here until morning.”
She stayed at his feet until morning and got up before people could recognize one another. Boaz said, “Let no one know that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
He said to her, “Bring the cloak you are wearing.” He took hold of it, measured six measures of barley into it, and put the load on her. Then she went into the town.
Ruth came to her mother-in-law, who said to her, “What is this, my daughter?” And she told her everything the man had done for her.
She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he told me, ‘Do not return empty-handed to your mother-in-law.’”
She said to her, “Stay here, my daughter, until you see that my word does not fail, for the man will not remain quiet or rest today until he has settled this matter.”

Boaz went up to the gate and sat there. The relative with the right of redemption, whom Boaz had mentioned, came passing by. Boaz said to him, “Turn aside and sit here so that we may talk.” So he turned aside and sat down.
Boaz took ten men from among the elders of the town and said to them, “Sit here.” And they sat down.
Boaz said to the relative with the right of redemption, “I am returning the portion of the fields belonging to our brother Elimelech to Naomi, who has come back from the land of Moab.

I have told you so that you may hear, saying, ‘Choose it for yourself before those seated here, before the elders, and before my people.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so that I may know, because you have the first right to redeem it, and I come after you.” He said to him, “Am I the one with the right of redemption?”

Boaz said to him, “When you acquire the fields from Naomi and from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the man who died, you must also take her, so that you may preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance.”
The relative with the right of redemption said, “I cannot redeem it, lest my own inheritance be lost. Exercise my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem it.”

This was formerly the rule in Israel concerning redemption and exchange: to confirm his word, a man would take off his sandal and give it to the other man who was exercising his right of redemption. This was the form of attestation in Israel.
The relative with the right of redemption said to Boaz, “Take my right of redemption for yourself.” He took off his sandal and gave it to him.
Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I have acquired from Naomi everything belonging to Elimelech and all the property of Chilion and Mahlon.

I have also taken Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, to be my wife, so that I may preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance, and so that the dead man’s name may not disappear from among his brothers or from the tribe of his people. You are my witnesses today.”

All the people at the gate said, “We are your witnesses.” The elders also said to him, “May the LORD make your wife, who is coming into your house, like Rachel and Leah, who together built the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and have a name in Bethlehem.
May your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman.”
Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. The LORD granted it to her, and she conceived and bore a son.
The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you today without a relative to redeem you, through whom your name will be known in Israel.
He will restore your life and sustain you in your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who bore him for you, loves you and is better to you than seven sons.”
Naomi took the child, laid him in her lap, and became his nurse.
Her neighbors gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi.” They named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
These are the descendants of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron.
Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab.
Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.
Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.
